mainTopic: Wine that sours after a sale, and the ברכה on drinks made from wine dregs
overview: This amud first finishes the argument between רב and שמואל about wine that sours right after it is sold. שמואל says the buyer's carrying shook the wine, so the loss is his. רב יוסף ruled like רב for beer and like שמואל for wine, and the הלכה follows שמואל. Then a ברייתא teaches that date beer, barley beer, and a drink made from wine dregs all get שהכל. אחרים say dregs that still taste like wine get בורא פרי הגפן, but רבה and רב יוסף rule against them. רבא explains with measurements. If three measures of water go in and four come out, everyone agrees it is wine. If three go in and three come out, everyone agrees it is not. They argue when three and a half come out, depending on how much water stays in the dregs. At the end, the גמרא challenges whether anyone would argue when more comes out than went in, and starts to quote a משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל: the wine soured on the buyer's shoulders
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that wine which sours soon after the sale is the buyer's loss, because carrying it shakes it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Wine gets shaken up on the shoulder of its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's side of the argument with רב, which began just before this line. שמואל says the souring happened after the sale, on the buyer's watch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is when the wine went bad: before the sale or after it. שמואל blames the buyer's carrying, which shakes the wine and makes it sour quickly. So the seller is not responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: Of its owner, meaning the new owner, the buyer

phrases.english: Wine gets shaken up on the shoulder of its owner.
phrases.notes: The "owner" here is the buyer carrying it home. The shaking is what makes it sour, so it is his loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing view to רב's statement, which comes just before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine that sours shortly after a sale is the buyer's responsibility, because carrying it shook it.

steps.title: רב יוסף's split ruling in real cases
steps.stepSummary: In actual cases, רב יוסף ruled like רב when the drink was beer and like שמואל when it was wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף ruled in a real case like רב with beer, and like שמואל with wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how רב יוסף actually judged real cases. He did not follow one side every time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With beer, רב יוסף followed רב, so the seller was responsible. With wine, he followed שמואל, so the buyer took the loss. The text does not explain the difference here. It only reports that he ruled this way.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled in a real case, as practice and not just theory
Like him, in agreement with his view

phrases.english: Rav Yosef ruled in an actual case

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the רב–שמואל argument was applied in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice: beer that sours is the seller's loss (like רב), and wine that sours is the buyer's loss (like שמואל).

steps.title: The הלכה follows שמואל
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling in the argument: the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the argument and רב יוסף's practice, the גמרא decides the law. Wine that sours after the sale is the buyer's loss, not the seller's.
steps.whatToRemember: Wine that sours soon after being sold: the הלכה follows שמואל. The buyer's carrying is blamed, so the seller is not responsible.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final ruling after the practical report
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל: the seller is not responsible for wine that sours after the sale.

steps.title: ברייתא: שהכל on date beer, barley beer, and wine-dregs drinks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that date beer, barley beer, and a drink made from wine dregs all get the ברכה of שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Whether it is date beer, barley beer, or wine dregs, we say over them the ברכה 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic tied to sour or weak drinks: which ברכה to make on them. The first opinion in the ברייתא says all three get שהכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the dregs come from grapes, the drink made from them is not treated as real wine. So it does not get בורא פרי הגפן. Like the beers, it gets the general ברכה of שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine dregs, the grape leftovers soaked in water to make a drink
The general ברכה: 'by Whose word all things came to be'

phrases.notes: He means the drink you get by soaking the leftover grape dregs in water.

phrases.english: we recite over them 'By Whose word all things came to be.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the ברכה on drinks that are like wine but not full wine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Date beer, barley beer, and a wine-dregs drink all get שהכל.

steps.title: אחרים: dregs with a wine taste get הגפן
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say that if the dregs drink still tastes like wine, it gets בורא פרי הגפן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: Dregs that have the taste of wine, one says over them 'בורא פרי הגפן'.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees about the wine dregs. If the drink still tastes like wine, its ברכה is הגפן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אחרים, the deciding factor is taste. If the wine flavor is still there, the drink counts as wine for the ברכה. The first opinion gives this kind of dregs drink only שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a named group of תנאים in the ברייתא
The ברכה on wine: 'Who creates the fruit of the vine'

phrases.english: dregs that have in them the taste of wine,
one recites over them 'Who creates the fruit of the vine.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion about wine dregs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dregs drink that tastes like wine gets בורא פרי הגפן.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: not like אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both rule against אחרים, so a dregs drink gets שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: The הלכה is not like אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים decide the argument in the ברייתא. They rule that the הלכה does not follow אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So even if the dregs drink tastes like wine, the ברכה stays שהכל, like the first opinion. A wine taste alone does not make it wine.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like this opinion

steps.whatToRemember: A drink made from wine dregs gets שהכל, even if it tastes like wine. The הלכה is not like אחרים.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
the halacha is not like Others.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ אֵין הֲלָכָה כַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions of the ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the first opinion: dregs drinks get שהכל.

steps.title: רבא: three in, four out, everyone agrees it is wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if three measures of water were poured on the dregs and four measures came out, all opinions agree it is real wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that if one poured in three and four came out, it is wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא limits the argument in the ברייתא. He gives one case where even the first opinion agrees the drink counts as wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If three measures of water went in and four came out, the extra measure must be real wine that was still in the dregs. That is one part wine to three parts water, which is enough to count as wine. The argument is only about weaker drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone, all opinions agree

steps.confusionAlert: This does not go against רבה and רב יוסף. They ruled about a normal dregs drink. רבא is describing a special case that everyone, even the first opinion, agrees is wine.

phrases.english: if he poured in three and four came out,
phrases.notes: Three measures of water were poured over the dregs, and after draining, four measures of drink came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the argument of the ברייתא by giving a case everyone agrees on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dregs drink where three measures of water produced four measures is real wine according to everyone.

steps.title: רבא is consistent with his view on diluting wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's ratio fits his other statement: wine that cannot take three parts water to one is not considered wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: Any wine that cannot carry three parts water to one is not wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's ruling fits with something else he said. This backs up the logic of his three-to-four case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that proper wine is so strong it should be mixed one part wine to three parts water. That is exactly the ratio in the dregs case: one part real wine to three parts water. So that mixture is normal drinking wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his other statement

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, normal wine is one part wine to three parts water. So a dregs drink that has that ratio counts as wine according to everyone.

phrases.english: any wine that does not carry

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 7 by showing it matches רבא's other known ruling
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a three-in, four-out dregs drink is wine
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's own statement that proper wine must be able to take three parts water to one

steps.title: Same amount in and out means it is not wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds the other end of the scale. If three measures of water were poured on the dregs and only three came out, everyone agrees the drink is not wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone poured three measures of water over the dregs and three measures came out, it is nothing. It does not count as wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his statement from step 7. Now he gives the case where everyone agrees the drink is NOT wine: the amount that comes out is the same as the amount poured in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, four out of three meant everyone agrees it is wine. Here, three out of three means no extra wine came out of the dregs, so it is just flavored water. With both ends set, רבא can now point to the middle case where the two sides argue.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing; it does not count

phrases.english: If one poured in three and three came out,

steps.triggerLanguage: רְמָא תְּלָתָא וַאֲתָא תְּלָתָא, וְלָא כְּלוּם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's range of cases. Step 7 gave the case where everyone agrees it is wine, and this gives the case where everyone agrees it is not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three in and three out: everyone agrees the drink is not wine.

steps.title: The disputed case and how רבנן see it
steps.stepSummary: The argument is when three go in and three and a half come out. רבנן say the three of water came back out, so only half a measure is wine, mixed into six halves of water. That is too weak to count as wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree when someone poured in three and three and a half came out. The רבנן hold that three went in and three came out, so half is left over. Half a measure of wine in six halves of water is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא identifies the exact case where רבנן and אחרים argue: three measures in, three and a half out. He then explains how רבנן do the math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן assume all the water that went in came back out, so only the extra half measure is real wine. That half measure is mixed with three measures of water, which is six halves, so the mix is 1 to 6. That is far weaker than the 1 to 3 limit from step 8, so it is not wine and gets שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: When do they disagree; the case they argue about
Went in (was soaked into the dregs)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, דִּרְמָא תְּלָתָא וַאֲתָא תְּלָתָא וּפַלְגָא –
phrases.english: When do they disagree? Where one poured in three and three and a half came out.
phrases.notes: "They" are the תנא קמא of the ברייתא and אחרים from steps 4–5.

phrases.english: three went in, three came out,

phrases.notes: That extra half jug is the only real wine that came from the dregs.

phrases.english: and a half in six halves of water

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, דִּרְמָא תְּלָתָא וַאֲתָא תְּלָתָא וּפַלְגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both ends are settled, רבא places the מחלוקת in the middle case and explains the רבנן's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three in and three and a half out: according to רבנן, only half a measure is wine in a 1:6 mix, so it is not wine.

steps.title: How אחרים see the disputed case
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say three measures soaked in but only two and a half came out. So a full measure of the drink is real wine, mixed with two and a half of water, and that counts as good wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים hold that three went in and two and a half came out, so a whole jug is left. A jug of wine in two and a half of water is good wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now explains the other side, אחרים, in the same case of three in and three and a half out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים assume some of the water stayed soaked in the dregs. Only two and a half measures of water came out, so a full measure of the result is real wine. One part wine to two and a half parts water is stronger than the 1 to 3 limit from step 8, so it counts as real wine and gets בורא פרי הגפן.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת is about how much water stays in the dregs. רבנן say none of it stays, so the mix is 1:6 and gets שהכל. אחרים say half a measure stays, so the mix is 1:2.5, which counts as wine and gets בורא פרי הגפן.

phrases.english: three went in, two and a half came out,
phrases.notes: Some of the water stays soaked in the dregs, taking the place of wine that comes out.

phrases.english: so a jug is left over;
and a jug in two and a half is wine,
phrases.notes: That is less water than the three-to-one limit from step 8, so it passes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲחֵרִים סָבְרִי: תְּלָתָא עוּל, תְּרֵין וּפַלְגָא נָפֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the מחלוקת set up in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אחרים, one measure of wine in two and a half of water is real wine.

steps.title: Do the Sages really argue when more comes out than went in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's setup. Would the חכמים argue at all when the drink that comes out is more than the water poured in? It starts to bring a משנה to show they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when more comes out than was poured in, do they really disagree? But we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a challenge against רבא's explanation and is setting up the next move: a quote from a משנה. The משנה itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא placed the מחלוקת in a case where three and a half came out of three, which is more than went in. The גמרא doubts that anyone would argue there, since extra liquid seems to show real wine came out. It is about to bring a משנה to prove that point.

keyTerms.meaning: More than its measure (more came out than was poured in)
But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: And where it is more than its measure, do they disagree?!
phrases.notes: "Its measure" means the amount of water poured in, like three in and three and a half out.
The quoted משנה is מעשרות 5:6, and it comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי מִדָּתוֹ, מִי פְּלִיגִי?! וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case רבא chose for the מחלוקת in steps 10–11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבנן and אחרים argue when three go in and three and a half come out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When more liquid comes out than went in, a משנה seems to treat the drink as wine without any argument. So placing the מחלוקת there looks impossible.
